summary: Session affinity reassignment during canary health window causes unexpected fallback to legacy variant
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary promote for redwood-7b-v2-quant, a subset of persistent sessions unexpectedly lost affinity and were routed to redwood-7b-v1 (legacy). Impact: A subset (~0.6% of requests for Fjord Analytics) experienced output divergence and increased latency for 18m during peak. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-west-2. Initial detection: customer reported mixed outputs in chat sessions and provided example session IDs. This ticket tracks the support/SRE investigation and mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a staged canary rollout of redwood-7b-v2-quant at 15% weight with session-affinity enabled (cookie TTL 1h).
2) Trigger rolling prewarm on 20 nodes while running continuous synthetic chat traffic with persistent cookies.
3) During the canary health window (health checks toggled to aggressive smoothing) observe routing decisions in edge-proxy logs and check variant assigned in orchestrator snapshot.
4) Reproduce by forcing an auth refresh from client to emulate token rotation observed in customer's environment.

(see full trace in linked GH issue and S3 logs)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Cookie mutation during auth refresh removed the edge cookie used for session affinity and accelerated fallback to a compatibility policy. Hypothesis B: During the canary health window we applied aggressive smoothing that allowed prewarm nodes to report transient degraded readiness; orchestrator's pin_reconcile deferred commits for affected cohort which caused a temporary affinity re-evaluation. Steps taken so far: collected edge-proxy traces, orchestrator snapshots, and prewarm health metrics. Correlated timestamps with customer-provided session IDs. Verified that when cookie mutation occurs concurrently with a health-probe state flip, orchestrator falls back to legacy variant due to conservative commit logic. We have replicated a reproduce in staging with synthetic auth refreshes and canary health smoothing enabled.

resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: adjusted health-smoothing parameters and allowed immediate pin_commit for sessions with active tenant cookies. No further fallbacks observed in customer's traffic after 2026-02-26 14:00 UTC. A code change (orchestrator PR #1842) prepared to make pin retention robust against concurrent auth refreshes. Postmortem and runbook updates scheduled.
root_cause: Race condition between edge cookie mutation during auth token refresh and orchestrator's canary health-window logic that defers pin commits. When both occurred, affinity lookup returned miss and routing policy fallback selected legacy variant.
follow_up_actions:
1) Merge and deploy orchestrator PR #1842 to ensure pin_commit for active-affinity sessions bypasses health-window deferral.
2) Add telemetry to detect cookie mutation events correlated with pin_reconcile deferrals.
3) Update Canary Health Window runbook to note auth-refresh interactions.
4) Notify customers with dedicated tenants of the fix and recommended client-side token refresh patterns.
